gaps.title: Victory is not a moment: no tally window, numbers land off-screen
gaps.detail: Measured in /index.html over ~40 fights. The instant the last monster pops, the screen becomes empty grass with the three party panels still up, and the entire payoff is one line at a time typed into the same big mostly-empty blue box that carried the combat log: 'The party gains 9 experience poin...' then '...and 3 gold coins.' There is no victory window, no held frame, no change of composition, nothing that says the fight is WON. Two floating gold numbers try to carry it and both fail: '+5 G' pops in dead centre over empty dirt with nothing under it, and '+3 EXP' pops at the far left where it is clipped by the screen edge and overlapped by Bram's HP panel (shots/P15-critic-d1/d/30-levelup-f16.png). Measured cost: 5.0 s from battle.phase==='victory' to standing on the lane, most of it staring at bare ground. DQV PS2 holds the battle frame, cuts the music to the fanfare, and puts the whole tally in ONE framed window - 'You have defeated the Slime! / Bram gains 9 experience points. / Bram receives 5 gold coins.' - then the level-up jingle. BUILD: a real victory window (same blue/pale-double-border stock as the command window) that slides in centre-screen on the pop of the last monster, holds while it fills line by line with EXP, gold and each drop, with the monsters' spots left empty behind it; anchor the +EXP/+G pops to where each monster actually died and clamp them inside the safe area so nothing clips; hold the frame for a beat before the ink curtain starts. NOTE: the level-up panel that follows (shots/P15-critic-d1/d/37-levelup-f23.png - 'Bram Level 2' with Max HP 26 +6 star, one stat revealed at a time) is genuinely good; the victory tally that leads into it is the hole.

events.note: Rebuilt as present.js victory(ev): a UI.window in the command window's own blue/pale-double-border stock, centre frame (top 186, min 560), title tab 'Victory!', sliding up on the last pop — and the combat-log box is CLOSED first, so the composition really changes. Experience then Gold COUNT UP (0..N over 380ms each, 340ms apart, a tick per row), then one line per drop. +EXP and +G are anchored to each monster's recorded death spot (state().battlePresent.deaths) and every pop is clamped into a safe rect (x 104..W-104, y 192..0.64H) so nothing clips the screen edge or lands under a party panel. Frame held 1.15s after it fills (Confirm fills it, Confirm again dismisses, first 0.32s unskippable), then 240ms of nothing, then the ink curtain. Measured in /index.html: phase victory -> tally window 2.72s (was 4.60s); victory -> standing on the lane 5.47s (was 6.69s; critic measured 5.0s of bare grass with no window at all). ALSO found the cause of '18px of plain unoutlined white' numerals: renderMarks() rebuilt the overlay every frame and re-appending a .dqb-pop restarted its CSS animation, freezing every numeral on keyframe 0 at scale .4 — pops now live in their own .dqb-pops layer that is never rebuilt, at 64px/900 weight with a 12-shadow ink outline ring, and they spring and float. Read shots/P15-r3/10-07-victory.png and shots/P15-index-r3/05-04b-victory-window.png + 04-04-the-hit.png. scenarios/P15.json and P15-index.json both exit 0 with new asserts on the window, the log and the pop geometry.

gaps.title: Battle presentation does not play any spell VFX
gaps.detail: src/art/fx.js (P20) now has 25 effects and src/data/spells.js gives every spell an fx id, an sfx id and a words template. present.js already sounds a spell (HOLD_SFX) but draws nothing. In createPresenter: import FX from ../art/fx.js, FX.attach(S.scene, {camera: S.camera, sound: sfx}) in buildStage, FX.update(dt) in the presenter tick, FX.setCamera(S.camera) when the camera moves, and on an act event of kind spell call FX.play(SPELLS[ev.spell].fx, {at: the target model's world position, scale: 0.7, sound: false, onPeak: () => the damage pop}). Scale 0.7 is right for the battle camera (0.55 up, 2.9 out) - at 1.0 a fire_big fills the frame. Also FX.play(defeat_poof) on a defeat event and FX.play(level_pillar) on the level-up, which is the ceremony the rubric asks for.

gaps.title: Nothing honours the fx.shake Bus event, so big spells do not move the camera
gaps.detail: src/art/fx.js emits Bus 'fx.shake' {amp (world units, 0.25-0.7), ms} at the peak of fire_big, lightning, frost, shockwave and level_pillar. The battle rig already has a shake field (battlePresent.camera.shake), so in present.js install: ctx.Bus.on('fx.shake', (p) => { S.shake = Math.max(S.shake, p.amp); }) and let it decay over p.ms. P09 should do the same for the field camera. Without it the heaviest spells land with no WEIGHT.
